Mathematically, this represents the earliest formalization of mapping a continuous random variable to a standardized percentile scale. The 'grades' (0 to 100) act as a discretized proxy for the cumulative distribution function (CDF). By tabulating specific values (e.g., height, weight, arm span) against these grades, the text implicitly defines a quantile function Q(g). The duality lies in treating these tables not merely as static records, but as generative kernels capable of synthesizing synthetic populations or evaluating outlier probabilities. Failure modes arise when the underlying population shifts drastically (secular trends in nutrition/health) or when the traits exhibit strong non-Gaussian dependencies not captured by simple marginal quantiles.
